source.title: Problems and Solutions in Nuclear and Particle Physics

raw_problem.problem_text: Explain in few lines, suggesting an example, how the knowledge of the proton range can be used to infer the range of another particle with different charge and mass.
raw_problem.solution_text: The quantity $z ^ { 2 } R / M$ (where $z$ is the charge in $e$ units, $R$ the range and $M$ the mass of the particle) is a universal function of $\beta \gamma = p / M .$ . As an example an $\alpha$ -particle having a kinetic energy $T _ { \alpha }$ has the same range of a proton with kinetic energy $T _ { p } = T _ { \alpha } / 4$ (same $\beta \gamma$ ), because $z _ { \alpha } ^ { 2 } / M _ { \alpha } = 1 / M _ { p }$ .
